If so we could start the first devnet soonish <@360491619402776577> I didn't check that balances went up in my interop, that's your problem if they don't 😛 I did check that the validators decreased balances in the beacon chain I'll try out the instructions and verify :) What do people think about removing `INVALID_BLOCK_HASH` status in a `newPayloadV2`? https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/270 <@755590043632140352> spec tests have been updated with the latest withdrawal process? want to have a go at it i haven't looked back into ethereumjs stateroot/blockhash not matching but withdrawal functionality minus the timestamp based forking is mostly implemented, looking to get lodestar ready for muli node interop not yet, but you can run the generator in my PR's branch. I'm hoping that will be merged today-ish and <@415109946682769408> will be generating the test-vectors I want to merge that before Danny comes back from vacations and starts requesting a bunch of changes, if it's already merged then it'll be someone else's problem 😄 I went over it and changed a couple of typos but also changed the command for prysmctl, take a look just in case. Thanks for writing this up why not start with shanghai at 0 with post merge genesis, would be really simple imho we can't start from a merged state I think <@833706406699073536> is working on that k understood <@755590043632140352> is MAX_WITHDRAWALS_PER_PAYLOAD for mainnet 8? i think your PR missed that value for mainnet preset ohh sorry its already there in the diff you changed value for minimal, so i didn't see any corresponding diff and assumed it was missing Oh it was reduced? I thought I had it at 16 minimal you reduced from 8 to 4 yeah minimal was reduced because the max at 8 would be enforced and that would be more than the max per epoch that was proposed before I think yea, thats ok, it got me confused about expecting a change for mainnet too 😆 self sorted I think it does, although could be clearer. There are some distinctions like ``` If withdrawal functionality is activated, client software MUST return an INVALID status with the appropriate latestValidHash if payload.withdrawals is null. Similarly, if the functionality is not activated, client software MUST return an INVALID status with the appropriate latestValidHash if payloadAttributes.withdrawals is not null. Blocks without withdrawals MUST be expressed with an explicit empty list [] value. ``` I don't think we should abuse INVALID status in this case. An error suites better IMO. I guess this is a line of code on EL side, like `if Capella then assert withdrawals are not nil else assert withdrawals are nil` I think invalid is good for us cause then we will mark the block as invalid and not allow continue on that branch. Also it doesn' t seem to change the semantics of it right? it's an invalid block from the pov of the EL Hmm yeah I think of it like "if withdrawals is non-nil, the CL thinks it is in the block and if it is nil, the CL thinks withdrawals aren't enabled" -- so it is less of an engine API error, rather, it's potentially telling the EL an invalid payload I am treating it as rather a miscommunication error between clients. CL is not capable of processing a block containing withdrawals before Capella, right? This block will be discarded with corresponding penalties applied to the remote peer if applicable. If EL is syncing and someone in the network gives it an EL block containing withdrawals the same should happen. Actually, in the latter case INVALID will be the response I guess 🤔 I guess in the case that you're describing CL should start complaining before making any Engine API call Considering a direct call to Engine API, an incorrect value for `withdrawals` field may only occur because of a bug in CL, and not because the payload was INVALID A bug in the CL may render the payload invalid. I mean I don't see much difference in the CL screwing up and sending an out of order withdrawal thus rendering the payload INVALID, vs the CL screwing up and sending a null withdrawal list. This is true, there could be endianness issue 😝 Or wei-gwei conversion issue. I am not insisting on the error, just trying to be sure that we don't abuse INVALID status for no reason <@755590043632140352> the way validatorIndex will be initiaized (from 0) and then used in withdrawals loop, the first validator probe will be on 1 not on 0th do we want to change semantics of validatorIndex in state to next to be probed validator (and adjust the loop accordingly?) It's commented on my PR, I dislike this less than the change in the spec to start at 0, to start at 0 you have to move the sum to the end of the loop and have twice the ugly construction of having to mod out by the number of validators ok, have been able to interop with geth on the without queue impl as well 🎉 <@755590043632140352> do you have some next setup where i can try to see if i can sync up the prysm nodes? that will sort of confirm if everything lines up, if no issues we can have multi client testnet <dannyryan> > <dannyryan> ha, I just reviewed the PR and suggested we start at 0 and do the mod twice... conforming these two vars to the same convention will greatly reduce chance of off-by-one errors and make thinking and talking about the feature simpler (re @amphora_interop_bot: <potuz> [reply]: It's commented on my PR, I dislike this less than the change in the spec to start at 0, to start at 0 you have to move the sum to the end of the loop and have twice the ugly construction of having to mod out by the number of validators) we talked about this with Alex, I don't feel strongly, but it is really awkward to have twice the moding out, I believe this approach is less prone to off-by-one errors, but I may be proven wrong. excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content:
I think it does, although could be clearer. There are some distinctions like 
```
If withdrawal functionality is activated, client software MUST return an INVALID status with the appropriate latestValidHash if payload.withdrawals is null. Similarly, if the functionality is not activated, client software MUST return an INVALID status with the appropriate latestValidHash if payloadAttributes.withdrawals is not null. Blocks without withdrawals MUST be expressed with an explicit empty list [] value.
```

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: I don't think we should abuse INVALID status in this case. An error suites better IMO. I guess this is a line of code on EL side, like `if Capella then assert withdrawals are not nil else assert withdrawals are nil`

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I think invalid is good for us cause then we will mark the block as invalid and not allow continue on that branch. Also it doesn' t seem to change the semantics of it right? it's an invalid block from the pov of the EL

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: Hmm yeah I think of it like "if withdrawals is non-nil, the CL thinks it is in the block and if it is nil, the CL thinks withdrawals aren't enabled" -- so it is less of an engine API error, rather, it's potentially telling the EL an invalid payload

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
I am treating it as rather a miscommunication error between clients.

CL is not capable of processing a block containing withdrawals before Capella, right? This block will be discarded with corresponding penalties applied to the remote peer if applicable. If EL is syncing and someone in the network gives it an EL block containing withdrawals the same should happen. Actually, in the latter case INVALID will be the response I guess 🤔

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: I guess in the case that you're describing CL should start complaining before making any Engine API call

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: Considering a direct call to Engine API, an incorrect value for `withdrawals` field may only occur because of a bug in CL, and not because the payload was INVALID

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: A bug in the CL may render the payload invalid. I mean I don't see much difference in the CL screwing up and sending an out of order withdrawal thus rendering the payload INVALID, vs the CL screwing up and sending a null withdrawal list.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: This is true, there could be endianness issue 😝  Or wei-gwei conversion issue. I am not insisting on the error, just trying to be sure that we don't abuse INVALID status for no reason
